business_problem: The Recording Academy needed more engaging digital experiences for fans and more personalized digital journeys for members because its brand increasingly depends on year-round online interactions, not just the Grammy Awards broadcast.
solution_summary: IBM and the Recording Academy combined agentic AI with CRM modernization to serve both fans and members. For fan engagement, the team used IBM watsonx and IBM watsonx Orchestrate to build GRAMMY IQ, where agentic workflows and AI assistants generate music-trivia questions, clues, and explanations from the Academy's proprietary data. The same data foundation also powers Musical Crossroads at the Grammy Museum, where generative AI creates bespoke narratives that explain relationships between artists and genres. On the member side, IBM Consulting used IBM Garage methods to redesign journeys across nominations, ticketing, voting, and renewals while modernizing Salesforce Experience Cloud and Salesforce Marketing Cloud. The combined architecture links proprietary content, orchestration, and CRM workflows so the Academy can create interactive fan experiences at scale while also simplifying multilingual member engagement and campaign operations.

data_flow: Recording Academy data feeds watsonx and watsonx Orchestrate for fan-facing AI experiences such as GRAMMY IQ, while member data flows through the modernized Salesforce Experience Cloud and Marketing Cloud stack to deliver personalized digital journeys and communications.
business_outcome: The Academy deepened fan engagement, made ticketing and maintenance more efficient, and created a more scalable personalized digital experience for members across channels and languages.
metrics: 2,500+ GRAMMY IQ questions generated about 200 nominees
architecture_clues: Proprietary music data is reused across multiple AI experiences rather than one campaign microsite.
The member platform integrates Salesforce CRM, Experience Cloud, and Marketing Cloud for a connected operating model.
The redesigned portal can be translated into Spanish, French, Portuguese, and Arabic far faster than before.
